subject: Trouble getting predicted values with new data

messages.author: e092355034cc4723
messages.subject: Trouble getting predicted values with new data
parts:
Hi Paul,

I am trying to get predicted and fitted values to be able to create my own plots for a model fit in brms, but I get the following error:
Error in tcrossprod(b, X) : non-conformable arguments

My model:

brmod <- brm(bf(Y ~ X * var1 * var2 + (1+X | group1) +
                (1| group2), sigma ~ X),
              data = dat, family = "gaussian",
              iter = 500, chains = 4, warmup = 200,
              cores = 4, save_model = "brm-mod-3.txt")

I created the newdata as;

dat1 <- as.data.frame(cbind(rep(seq(from = 0, to = max(dat$X),
                                length.out = 50), times = 16),
                      rep(levels(dat$var1), each = 200),
                      rep(levels(dat$var2), times = 4, each = 50)))

Then, I used:

pp.brm <- predict(brmod, newdata = dat1,  re_formula = NA, scale = "linear")

Does the "non-conformable" error mean that there is a discrepancy in the how the factor levels are labelled when the model is compiled versus the actual specified labels in the data?
Could the error be related to estimating 'sigma' in the model?

Thanks,
Meghna

messages.author: 6e3dd74b422c061b
messages.subject: Re: [brms-users] Trouble getting predicted values with new data
parts:
Indeed that tells us that the number of fixed effects is not the same as at fitting time. If this is caused by some misspecification of the user, it should result in an informative error message. Whenever, this "crossprod" thing pops up, it it likely a bug in brms.

What version of brms are you using? Could you retry it with brms 1.8.0 (latest release from CRAN)?

If it is still not working, would you mind providing a reproducible example possibly with some fake data?

Many thanks!
Paul

messages.subject: Re: [brms-users] Re: Trouble getting predicted values with new data
parts:
Hi Paul,

I realized the problem! I was creating the new data using as.data.frame(cbind(...)) which was converting all variables to factors. If I instead create the new data as:

dat1 <- data.frame(X = rep(seq(from = 0, to = max(dat$X),
length.out = 50), times = 16),

var1 = rep(levels(dat$var1), each = 200),
                      var2 = rep(levels(dat$var2), times = 4, each = 50))

then, predict() works fine.

Thanks for your time!

Best,
Meghna
